text_blocks.snippet: A 103°F (39.4°C) fever in adults can be a cause for concern and warrants medical attention, especially if accompanied by other symptoms like confusion, difficulty breathing, or loss of consciousness. While fevers are a natural response to infection, persistent high fevers can potentially lead to complications like dehydration and strain on organs. If you have a fever of 103°F or higher, it's recommended to contact a healthcare provider.
snippet_highlighted_words: confusion, difficulty breathing, or loss of consciousness

list.title: High fever:
list.snippet: A fever of 103°F (39.4°C) or higher in adults should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.

list.title: Accompanying symptoms:
list.snippet: If the fever is accompanied by confusion, difficulty breathing, loss of consciousness, severe headache, stiff neck, or other concerning symptoms, seek immediate medical care.

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: If the fever persists for more than a few days despite treatment, or if you have a fever that keeps recurring, consult a doctor.

list.title: Other health conditions:
list.snippet: Individuals with pre-existing conditions like heart problems, weakened immune systems, or other chronic illnesses should seek medical advice promptly if they develop a fever.
Monitor your temperature: Use a reliable thermometer to track your temperature.
Rest and fluids: Get plenty of rest and stay hydrated by drinking fluids.
Over-the-counter medications: Consider taking over-the-counter fever reducers like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) according to package directions.
Avoid aspirin in children and teens: Aspirin should not be given to children or teenagers due to the risk of Reye's syndrome.
Consult your doctor: If your fever is high or doesn't respond to treatment, contact your doctor for further guidance.

list.title: Fever is a symptom, not a disease:
list.snippet: Fever is the body's natural response to infection, helping to fight off illness.

list.title: Brain damage is rare:
list.snippet: While very high fevers (above 107.6°F or 42°C) can potentially cause brain damage, this is very rare, especially in the context of fever due to infection.

list.title: Individual response:
list.snippet: People react differently to fever, and some may feel more uncomfortable than others at the same temperature.

list.title: Seek medical advice for specific situations:
list.snippet: If you have any concerns about your fever, especially if you have other health conditions, it's always best to consult with a healthcare professional for personalized advice.
